newsitem.title: USA: Air Force confirms $2 billion F-22 cost overrun.
newsitem.headline: Air Force confirms $2 billion F-22 cost overrun.

text.p: The Air Force confirmed Tuesday a $2 billion cost overrun in development of its F-22 stealth fighter plane but said fixes will prevent further overruns estimated as high as $15 billion.
"We solved that cost growth problem and the alleged production problem is not there," Air Force Chief of Staff Ronald Fogleman told reporters after a Senate hearing.
The F-22 is being developed by Lockheed Martin and Boeing.

Fogleman made the comments after a Senate Armed Services Committee hearing at which Sen. John Warner, a Virginia Republican, said an Air Force study projected possible F-22 cost overruns of $6 billion to $13 billion. Warner said an upcoming Defence Department report will estimate possible overruns of $15 billion.
Warner said the cost overrun will require the Air Force to build 54 fewer F-22s in the first five years, less than 70 rather than the 120 planned.
Fogleman said the initial overrun was $2.14 billion.
He did not give a detailed answer at the hearing but told reporters the Air Force and Lockheed have already signed an agreement that will prevent the additional overruns of up to $15 billion overrun.

He said the memorandum of understanding requires Lockheed and Boeing to carry out efficiencies to keep costs of the plane from rising even though production will be slowed down, which normally increases overall costs.

The radar-evading F-22 is be the Air Force's chief fighter plane at the start of the next century and Fogleman told senators the country cannot afford to scrap it despite the high cost of three new warplanes under development.
